redFirst.basis: `python3 tests/test__worktrees.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 on "AttributeError: module '_worktrees' has no attribute 'advance_tree'" (read as python), and the task introduces 'advance_tree': absent from HEAD's module-level bindings of plugins/audit/scripts/git/_worktrees.py and bound in the working tree's; a second run with the working tree's implementation copied in exited 0 without that error, its tests reaching their assertions; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, OLDPWD, PWD; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; no .npmrc to carry or drop

outcome.technical: Attempt 5 enforces two invariants rather than patching the one path the review found. (1) KEPT IS DERIVED: advance_tree and advance_task_tree are now wrappers whose answer's `kept` is read off the disk at the end (_with_kept/_left_beside: the copy or its tombstone where one stands, else None; an error is added when something is left and none was said). The inner _advance/_advance_task never set kept. _drop_copy returns '' or why (rename and both rmtrees inside one try), _settle and every resume branch carry that text, and a tombstone that cannot be cleared refuses the move. (2) NEVER FORCE OVER UNKNOWN BYTES: _resume first runs _newer_work for both copy branches. HEAD must be a commit the move stood on; each work path must read as the copy holds it; every changed path must be work, a record (the copy's non-work paths plus the caller's is_record, now passed into _resume), or a moved path reading as the other commit's blob (_reads_as: rev-parse commit:path against hash-object). Anything else keeps the copy, changes nothing and names the paths. The end==base branch no longer uses the exact-status match: after the comparison it only drops. Finishing uses _answers_as with an is_record allowance, so refreshed records are no fault. (3) FSYNC: _keep_copy writes each bin and the git index through _write_synced (flush+fsync), fsyncs the directory, writes index.json through _write_aside (which now fsyncs before its rename), then fsyncs the directory again before anything moves. _fsync_dir does nothing on Windows, which will not open a directory to sync it. drive-phase.py: only advance_member's docstring changed; the stop is still `if said["kept"]`. Tests: av32-av40 new; av27 rewritten. Red on the attempt-4 code (saved at <scratchpad>/a4-snapshot) before the fix: av32, av33, av34 and av35 (the newer a.txt/c.txt bytes were lost), av36 (exact-status refusal), av38 (index.json never written aside, no fsync); ab7 and ab8 (the drive went on, gated and removed the tree); av27 (the _write_synced point missing; its 108 kills otherwise settled). av37 was green on attempt-4 and av39/av40 were written later; all three are proved by mutation. Final runs, each exit 0: test__worktrees 153/153, test_drive_phase 583/583, test_manage_worktrees 74/74, test__filed_returns 117/117, test__deps 254/254, test__output_lints 169/169, ruff, vermin, gate 2/2 files 736 cases.
outcome.descriptive: Whether a tree is settled is now read off the disk, and a leftover copy is never forced over work it does not account for; the p10 data loss is closed by an invariant.

testsAdded: av32-av33: the copy's rename refused after a counted move and after an undone one -> kept names the copy still on disk
av34: the reviewer's p10 end to end - failed drop, newer edits to a.txt and the tracked c.txt, next move: no byte changes, kept, both paths named
av35: newer edits after a kill and before the next move -> the same hold
av36 ALLOW: a recorded move whose copy stayed, records refreshed, work as copied -> copy dropped, settled
av37: the same with newer work -> held and named
av38: copy files and directory fsynced before index.json, index.json and the directory before the first checkout
av39 ALLOW / av40: git's checkout left part way (a moved file at the head's bytes) is undone and moved; a moved file holding bytes neither commit has is held

av27 rewritten: every call counted on an unarmed run then armed in turn, across a plain move, the undoing and finishing resume after a first kill, and a failing move's own undo; git armed before and after each writing call; a bigger work set; holds allowed only where the copy holds the work and a further move changes nothing
ab7/ab8: a copy that will not come down stops the drive after a counted move and after an undone move, with no gate row
